atoms.text: Next, Carla is going to show you around some buildings in hot areas around the world.

instruction.text: Select the three images of houses in hot areas.

finish.text: Great! Houses in hot areas are often made of mud, adobe (a type of brick made from mud) or stone. These materials are great at keeping houses cool in hot weather.
finish.sound: Great! Houses in hot areas are often made of mud, adobe, a type of brick made from mud, or stone. These materials are great at keeping houses cool in hot weather.

feedback.wrong: This is an igloo in a cold area.

instruction.text: This is a building on the Greek island of Santorini. Select the biggest blue dome to learn more.

feedback.end: This is a church made of mud, stone and volcanic cement. It has been painted white, like most other Greek houses. This helps keep the inside cool because light colours reflect heat.

instruction.text: This is a mud house in a Nubian village in Egypt. Select the staircase to learn more.

feedback.end: Houses in hot areas are often much more open than houses in the UK, so you can enjoy the warm sunshine. The bright colours and decorations show the Nubian people’s culture.

instruction.text: These are adobe houses in a Native American town in the USA. Select the walls to learn more.

feedback.end: Adobe is made from earth and other natural materials and is known for being sturdy and easy to use. Adobe houses are commonly found in hot and dry areas around the world.

instruction.text: Do houses in hot areas usually have the following? Select the correct answer.

feedback.finish: Although houses around the world look different depending on people’s culture and what materials are available, they also have similarities when built for similar kinds of weather!

instruction.text: Let’s do some fieldwork! Carla wants to use a map to find where adobe houses might be in the USA. Select the correct image.

feedback.end: Correct! Sandy colours on a map show that an area is dry. Adobe houses are built for hot and dry areas, so you might find them here.

hint.text: Sandy colours on a map show a hotter desert area!

instruction.text: You and Carla have arrived at an adobe house and want to see how it’s built for hot weather. Answer Carla’s question.

atoms.a: “What tool could we use to measure the temperature inside and outside the house?“
atoms.sound: ssml:<voice voiceLang='en' voice='f8_2025'>What tool could we use to measure the temperature inside and outside the house?</voice>

feedback.correct: Nice! You can use a thermometer to measure temperatures.

atoms.a: “Do you think the inside or outside will be a cooler temperature?”
atoms.sound: ssml:<voice voiceLang='en' voice='f8_2025'>Do you think the inside or outside will be a cooler temperature?</voice>

feedback.end: Exactly! Adobe keeps the inside of the house cool when it’s really hot outside.
